according to the geometry relationship between the corresponding first-/last-bounce scatterer (i.e., 1st/2nd point associated with cluster) and the element. Specifically, the delay and angle of a ray generated according to current TR 38.901 [3] can be treated as the observed delay and angle at the reference antenna element, which is used to locate the first-/last-bounce scatterer, and the observed delay and angle at other antenna elements can be subsequently calculated after scatterer locating. Figure 1 Illustration of near-field modelling methodology Following is the 38.901-based step-wise channel coefficient generation procedure taking aforementioned near-field modelling methodology into consideration: Step 1-10: Generate the delays, angles, and initial phases for a pair of reference antenna elements. Step 10.5: For each ray: Locate the first-/last-bounce scatterer. The scatterer locating approach in the section 3.4 of [4] can be referred to, which is described detailedly in Appendix A. Calculate the observed angle at each antenna element as well as the distances between the first-/last-bounce scatterer and each antenna element. Step 11-12: Generate channel coefficients according to formula (1)-(3) and apply pathloss and shadowing. (1) (2) (3) where represents the distance between Tx reference antenna element and Rx reference antenna element, represents the distance between the last-bounce scatterer and Rx reference antenna element , represents the distance between the first-bounce scatterer and Tx reference antenna element, and represents the propagation delay from Tx reference antenna element to Rx reference antenna element through the NLOS path (n, m). Proposal 1: For the near-field propagation model of direct and non-direct path, the channel coefficient should be generated according to formulas (1)-(3). Some companies questioned that the aforementioned near-field modelling methodology cannot match the reflection characteristics. For example, as shown in the left part of Figure 2, when there exists a reflection surface in the propagation environment close to the BS/UE side, locating the first-/last-bounce scatterer at the dashed circle position will lead to inaccurate spherical-wavefront. While we don’t think constructing the precise correspondence between stochastic channel model and deterministic propagation environment is that meaningful, even if a company insists to do so, the stochastically generated scatterer locating at the image position shown in Figure 2 should meet their requirement. Figure 2 Propagation environment with reflection surface

Specifically, the delay and angle of a ray generated according to current TR 38.901 [3] can be treated as the observed delay and angle at the reference antenna element, which is used to locate the first-/last-bounce scatterer, and the observed delay and angle at other antenna elements can be subsequently calculated after scatterer locating. Figure 2 Illustration of near-field modelling methodology Following is the 38.901-based step-wise channel coefficient generation procedure taking aforementioned near-field modelling methodology into consideration: Step 1-10: Generate the delays, angles, and initial phases for a pair of reference antenna elements. Step 10.5: For each ray: Locate the first-/last-bounce scatterer. The scatterer locating approach in the section 3.4 of [4] can be referred to, which is described detailedly in Appendix A. Calculate the observed angle at each antenna element as well as the distances between the first-/last-bounce scatterer and each antenna element. Notice that here we haven’t modelled per-element doppler shift and delay. documents.text: nfigured M = 1 or 4 sample measurement is applicable to all the concurrent NR positioing measurement methods and all frequency layers. Rel-17 also specified first path RSRP measurement: DL PRS-RSRPP. But the text in current 38.214 states that M = 1 or 4 sample is only appliable to DL RSTD, DL PRS-RSRP and UE Rx-Tx time difference measurement, but not to DL PRS-RSRPP. That would cause misunderstanding that the configured M = 1or 4 sample measurement is not applicable to DL PRS-RSRPP measurement.
